name: International courier and shipping
summary: How expats ship documents and parcels in and out of Singapore — passport/visa pouches, school applications, and household goods vs courier limits — without mixing formal customs rules with Facebook “runner” risk.
body:
Couriers move time-critical documents (visa packets, apostilles, school transcripts) and small parcels when full movers are overkill. Singapore’s retail courier network is dense; quality differences show up in customs brokerage, prohibited-item advice, and tracking clarity.

## Use cases
- Passport renewal packs to embassies abroad / returns
- Notarised or apostilled documents to home-country authorities
- University and school application packets with deadlines
- Phone/laptop RMA to regional service hubs
- Care packages within airline and courier restricted lists

For door-to-door furniture, use movers/relocation — couriers are not cheap mini-containers.

## Compliance basics
Declare accurately. Batteries, food, medicines, and brand-parallel goods trigger holds. HSA/AVA-adjacent items are not “just declare as gifts.” Personal document shipments still need correct receiver ID details.

## How to choose
Compare door-to-door vs service-point dropoff, insurance limits, and whether duties are billed as DDP/DDU. For passports, prefer carriers used to embassy pouches and signature-on-delivery. Avoid informal runners for valuables or immigration documents.

## Practical tip
Photograph contents and tracking labels before handover. For deadline filings, build two courier buffer days — tropical storms and customs queries are normal, not exceptional.
whenToEngage: Shipping passports or apostilled docs on a deadline
School/university packet needs tracked international delivery
Unsure courier vs mover for small household goods
Quoted informal runner for immigration documents
